topSignals.title: MISO's self-committed deadline to file its large-load interconnection tariff with FERC is today — no filing confirmed as of this check, for the second day running.
topSignals.text: MISO told stakeholders it would file the Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements Tariff with FERC "before end of August 2026," responding to the June 18 six-RTO show-cause order (the earlier 60-day justification deadline was August 17; the substantive tariff-revision filing is the one due today). No ER26-docket filing or MISO press confirmation found yet — carries over unresolved into September. MISO Large Load Interconnection | Akin Gump

topSignals.title: NuScale's much-discussed TVA mega-deal is a financing structure, not a NuScale-owned fleet — a distinction not previously spelled out in this digest.
topSignals.text: Reporting on the up-to-6-8 GW NuScale/TVA/Entra1 SMR program (still a non-binding September 2025 MOU, PPA not yet signed) clarifies that Entra1 Energy — not NuScale — would finance and own the reactors, selling output to TVA under future PPAs; NuScale's role is technology licensing/supply. Relevant for comparing SOFC's simpler owner-operator or PPA models against SMR's more complex financing stack when the two compete for the same data-center load. Motley Fool | Inside Climate News

topSignals.title: Priority-stack check: Elcogen and Topsoe both confirmed quiet for a second straight day.
topSignals.text: Elcogen's newsroom shows nothing since the August 3 Insight piece (interview on manufacturing-style scaling); ELCO I Tallinn remains in volume production at 360 MW/yr. Topsoe's press room shows nothing beyond the already-logged August 27 H1 2026 results (Company Announcements 10/2026 and 11/2026). No new SOFC/SOEC product, factory, partnership, or funding news from either priority stack. Elcogen News | Topsoe News

items.text: Other players: No new stack/cell-level announcements found today from Bloom, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, Sunfire, or Convion. Background check on SolydEra/Convion and Mitsubishi/Kyocera turned up only pre-existing partnerships (SolydEra-Convion 2023 tie-up) and market-report boilerplate — nothing dated to the last 24–48h.
MISO large-load tariff filing: Deadline is today — see Top Signal #1.

Germany EnEfG: PUE-relaxation detail from August 30 stands; Bundestag/Bundesrat passage still expected this autumn, and the reporting-threshold question (>23.6 GWh/>1 MW vs. 500 kW installed-IT-power) remains unreconciled.
Texas ERCOT audit: Unchanged, still targeting ~December 10, 2026 completion.
Project Jupiter (NM): Supreme Court response due September 2 — see AI Data Center Deployments above.

SMR reality check (Inside Climate News, Aug 30): As of August 2026, zero SMRs are commercially deployed in the US; of 22 designs under development (per Third Way), only two — both NuScale's — hold NRC design approval. Texas Gov. Abbott's early-August pause on new data-center approvals (cited as a lack of energy and water) prompted NuScale's CEO to pitch SMRs as the fix the next day on its Q2 call — illustrates SMR vendors positioning against the same grid/water bottlenecks SOFC already addresses on a 90-day deployment timeline. Inside Climate News
NuScale/TVA/Entra1 ownership structure: See Top Signal #2 — financing complexity (three-party structure, non-binding MOU, no signed PPA) versus SOFC's simpler on-balance-sheet or PPA-direct models.

Rolls-Royce SMR GDA: Still targeting "August 2026" completion per its own published Step-3 timeline; no Design Acceptance Confirmation/Statement of Design Acceptability found granted as of today. Given the month ends today, this is now the item to watch first in September.
Gas turbines, grid-scale batteries, PEM/hydrogen: no new dated developments.

Bloom Energy (BE): No new trading session data beyond Friday August 28's close ($228.11, per the August 28 digest entry, following the Mizuho/Clear Street upgrades). Recent range this month: ~$157 low to ~$248 high. No new catalyst identified today.
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Q3 FY2026 results call remains confirmed for September 2, 10:00 a.m. ET — nothing new today.

Ceres Power (CWR.L): Share price 410.12p as of August 28 (+1.56% that session); its subsidiary RFC Power (manganese flow battery, long-duration storage) closed a £10M Series A on August 26 with British Business Bank, Centrica, Ceres, and Temasek Trust participating — reduces Ceres' RFC Power stake to ~37%. Diversification move, not core SOFC news, but relevant to Ceres' capital allocation. Investing.com
Topsoe: Nothing beyond the already-logged August 27 H1 2026 results.

lcoe.text: No new capex/opex/efficiency figures today. The Nature Communications modular-SOFC LCOE figure ($0.155/kWh, hybrid series-parallel design, four-scale-up-strategy comparison) noted above is ✎ background-only for this digest — it predates the window and needs cross-checking against whether it's already in [[inocel-systemparameter-rechner]] or the LCOE model before use, not treated as a new input here.
